subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For long Codex-backed channel maintenance turns interrupted by app-server close or Gateway restart, should OpenClaw resume the turn, synthesize a recovery/status message, or fail closed with clearer interruption copy?
rationale: The source path is real, but the correct behavior crosses replay safety, side-effecting maintenance work, Gateway shutdown semantics, and channel delivery guarantees, so automation should not choose the policy unilaterally.

options.title: Resume or notify through restart recovery
options.body: Use existing restart markers and Codex resume/interrupt contracts to continue when safe, otherwise send an explicit restart-interruption notice to the original channel.

options.title: Fail closed with clearer classification
options.body: Keep replay conservative and only improve user-facing copy so Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server closure, and retry exhaustion are distinguishable.

options.title: Defer restart until active turns drain
options.body: Make managed restarts wait for active Codex turns to deliver or timeout before shutting down, accepting longer operator restart latency.

recommendation.title: Resume or notify through restart recovery
recommendation.body: Use existing restart markers and Codex resume/interrupt contracts to continue when safe, otherwise send an explicit restart-interruption notice to the original channel.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent cross-surface history in both Codex attempt lifecycle and reply delivery, which makes them the best available routing owner for the product-policy choice.
